topics.title: Review of JSS 2 Work
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to explain basic circuit components, list three entrepreneurship skills in computer repairs, and identify two software tools used in GSM servicing.

Introduction:
We have learned about basic circuits and computer parts in JSS 2. Today we will review these important topics to build our knowledge for more advanced repairs.

Content:
Basic circuits are the foundation of all electronic devices. They consist of components like resistors, capacitors, and transistors that control electricity flow. For example, when you charge your phone, current flows through circuits made of these components. Entrepreneurship skills in computer repairs include customer service, pricing your services fairly, and keeping good records. Like when a student brings a damaged phone to your repair shop in Lagos, you need to explain the problem clearly and charge a reasonable price. Software tools we used include multimeters to measure electricity and oscilloscopes to see electrical signals. These tools help us find problems in phones like when a Nokia phone won't turn on.

Class activity:
Students will work in pairs to identify different circuit components on a motherboard and explain their function.

Evaluation questions:
1. Name three components found in basic circuits.
2. Why is good customer service important for a computer repair business?
3. How does a multimeter help in GSM repairs?
4. What might be wrong if a phone gets hot during charging?

Summary:
Today we reviewed circuit components, entrepreneurship skills, and software tools that will help us in our advanced GSM repairs this term.

topics.title: Introduction to Advanced GSM Repairs
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to identify advanced GSM faults, differentiate between board-level and component-level repairs, and explain the tools needed for board-level repairs.

Introduction:
After reviewing basic components, we now move to more complex phone problems. These advanced faults require special skills and tools to fix.

Content:
Advanced GSM faults are problems that cannot be solved by simply replacing parts. For example, when a phone has no power even with a new battery, this is an advanced fault. Board-level repairs mean fixing the main circuit board of the phone, called the motherboard. This is different from component-level repairs where you just change one part. To do board-level repairs, you need special tools like a hot air rework station to remove components without damaging the board. You also need a microscope to see tiny parts on the board. In Nigeria, many phones suffer from water damage which can cause advanced faults on the board. Like when a student's phone falls into a bowl of soup during lunch, the corrosion on the board needs special cleaning and repair techniques.

Class activity:
Students will examine damaged motherboards and identify possible faults using magnifying glasses and multimeters.

Evaluation questions:
1. What is the difference between board-level and component-level repairs?
2. Name two tools needed for board-level repairs.
3. Why is water damage a common problem in Nigerian phones?
4. How would you approach a phone that turns on but has no display?

Summary:
Advanced GSM repairs require special skills and tools to fix complex problems on phone motherboards.

topics.title: Soldering and Desoldering Techniques
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to list soldering tools, explain safety precautions when soldering, and demonstrate proper soldering and desoldering techniques.

Introduction:
To repair modern phones, we must be able to attach and remove small electronic parts. This requires learning proper soldering and desoldering techniques.

Content:
Soldering tools include a soldering iron, solder wire, flux, and a desoldering pump or wick. The soldering iron heats up to melt the solder that holds components in place. Solder wire is made of tin and lead that flows when heated to create strong electrical connections. Flux helps the solder flow better and prevents oxidation. Safety precautions are very important when soldering. Always wear safety glasses to protect your eyes from splashes. Work in a well-ventilated area because soldering fumes can be harmful. Use a heat-resistant mat to protect your table. Never touch the hot soldering iron tip. In Nigeria, during the harmattan season, static electricity can damage sensitive components, so always use an anti-static wrist strap. When soldering, heat the component pad and the component leg simultaneously, then apply solder. For desoldering, first heat the existing solder until it melts, then use the desoldering pump to remove it.

Class activity:
Students will practice soldering and desoldering components on practice boards using proper safety equipment.

Evaluation questions:
1. Name three tools needed for soldering.
2. Why is ventilation important when soldering?
3. What is the purpose of flux in soldering?
4. Describe the proper technique for desoldering a component.

Summary:
Proper soldering and desoldering techniques are essential skills for any GSM repair technician, and safety must always come first.

topics.title: Replacing Phone Components
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to identify different phone components, explain the procedure for replacing each component, and demonstrate the safe removal and installation of phone parts.

Introduction:
Now that we know how to solder, we can learn to replace common phone parts that get damaged. These repairs are among the most frequent in phone repair shops across Nigeria.

Content:
Common phone components that need replacement include charging ports, screens, speakers, and buttons. The charging port is where you plug in the charger. When it gets loose or stops working, you need to replace it. First, remove the phone's back cover and battery. Then disconnect the charging port connector from the motherboard. Desolder the old port and solder the new one in its place. Screens often crack when phones fall, like when a student's phone slips from their hand in a crowded market. To replace a screen, heat the screen to soften the adhesive, carefully remove the broken screen, clean the old adhesive, and install the new screen. Speakers can fail from water damage or dust. To replace a speaker, open the phone, locate the speaker, disconnect it, and install the new one. Buttons can wear out with use. When replacing power buttons, be careful with small connectors and ribbon cables that are very delicate.

Class activity:
Students will work in groups to practice replacing different components on old, non-working phones.

Evaluation questions:
1. What are the steps to replace a phone charging port?
2. Why is it important to be careful with ribbon cables when replacing parts?
3. How does water damage affect phone speakers?
4. What safety precautions should you take when replacing a phone screen?

Summary:
Replacing phone components requires careful handling and proper techniques to avoid causing more damage to the device.

topics.title: Mid-Term Examination
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to demonstrate their understanding of GSM repair concepts through written and practical examination.

Introduction:
Today we will have our mid-term examination to assess your knowledge of the topics we have covered so far this term.

Content:
The examination will cover the review of JSS 2 work, introduction to advanced GSM repairs, soldering and desoldering techniques, and replacing phone components. The written section will include multiple choice, short answer, and practical problem-solving questions. For the practical section, you will demonstrate your ability to identify faults on a phone motherboard and show proper soldering techniques. Remember to follow all safety procedures during the practical exam. The exam is designed to test both your theoretical knowledge and hands-on skills, which are both essential for becoming a competent GSM repair technician.

Class activity:
Students will complete the mid-term examination consisting of written and practical components.

Evaluation questions:
The examination questions will serve as the evaluation for this week.

Summary:
The mid-term examination allows us to measure your progress and identify areas that need more attention as we continue with the term's work.

topics.title: Troubleshooting Advanced Faults
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to identify power IC faults, diagnose CPU-related problems, and troubleshoot memory issues in mobile devices.

Introduction:
After our mid-term break, we return to more complex phone problems. Today we will learn how to find and fix advanced faults that happen inside the phone's main processor and memory systems.

Content:
Power IC faults occur when the part that manages electricity to the phone stops working properly. Symptoms include the phone not turning on, getting very hot, or shutting down randomly. To diagnose a power IC problem, first check if the battery is good. Then test the voltage at different points on the motherboard using a multimeter. If the voltage is missing where it should be, the power IC may be damaged. CPU-related problems happen when the phone's processor has issues. Symptoms include the phone freezing, running very slow, or not starting up properly. To diagnose CPU problems, you may need to use specialized equipment to test the processor signals. Memory issues occur when the phone's RAM or storage has problems. Symptoms include apps crashing, the phone restarting itself, or files becoming corrupted. To diagnose memory issues, you can run diagnostic software if available, or test by replacing the memory chip if you suspect it's faulty.

Class activity:
Students will work with faulty phones to diagnose power IC, CPU, and memory issues using appropriate testing equipment.

Evaluation questions:
1. What are three symptoms of a faulty power IC?
2. How can you test for CPU-related problems?
3. What memory issues might a phone with corrupted files have?
4. Why is it important to check the battery first when diagnosing power issues?

Summary:
Troubleshooting advanced faults requires systematic testing and knowledge of how the phone's main components work together.

topics.title: Mid-Term Break
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to rest and prepare for the second half of the term.

Introduction:
This is a break from classes to allow students and teachers to rest and recharge for the remaining part of the term.

Content:
Mid-term break is a time for rest and revision. Students should use this time to review the topics covered so far and practice their repair skills. It is also a good time to observe how phone repair shops in your community handle different types of faults. Take notes on common problems and how they are fixed. This practical observation will help you understand real-world repair scenarios better than just classroom learning. Remember to stay safe during the break and avoid attempting complex repairs without proper supervision.

Class activity:
No formal class activity during the break. Students are encouraged to rest and review previous topics.

Evaluation questions:
No formal evaluation during the break period.

Summary:
The mid-term break provides an opportunity for rest and revision to prepare for the second half of the term's work.

topics.title: Flashing and Unlocking Complex Devices software bricking
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to explain the process of flashing Android and iPhones, describe IMEI repair procedures, and identify methods to avoid software bricking.

Introduction:
Today we learn about software issues that can make phones unusable and how to fix them without replacing hardware parts.

Content:
Flashing is the process of reinstalling the phone's operating system. This is needed when the software becomes corrupted or damaged. For Android phones, flashing involves using tools like SP Flash Tool or Odin to install a new firmware. For iPhones, it requires using special software like iTunes or 3uTools. IMEI repair is fixing the phone's unique identification number that sometimes gets lost during improper flashing. This is important because networks use IMEI to identify stolen phones. Software bricking happens when the phone's software becomes so corrupted that it won't turn on at all. This can happen if you turn off the phone during flashing or use incompatible firmware. To avoid bricking, always back up important data before flashing, use the correct firmware for the exact phone model, and ensure stable power supply during the process. In Nigeria, many phones need flashing when they develop software issues after being repaired or when changing from one network to another.

Class activity:
Students will practice flashing a test device with prepared firmware under supervision.

Evaluation questions:
1. What is flashing and why is it sometimes necessary?
2. How is IMEI repair different from regular software flashing?
3. What are three common causes of software bricking?
4. Why is it important to use the correct firmware when flashing a phone?

Summary:
Flashing and unlocking are advanced software repair techniques that require careful execution to avoid damaging the device.

topics.title: Practical: Complex Fault Repair
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to diagnose multiple phone faults, apply appropriate repair techniques, and document the repair process systematically.

Introduction:
Today we put all our knowledge into practice by repairing phones with multiple complex faults, just like in a real repair shop in Onitsha or Lagos.

Content:
Complex fault repair involves phones with multiple problems at the same time. For example, a phone might have a broken screen, a faulty charging port, and software issues all at once. The first step is to make a complete list of all the problems before starting repairs. Then prioritize the repairs - usually software issues should be fixed before hardware problems. When working on multiple faults, it's important to test the phone after each repair to ensure you haven't introduced new problems. Document each step of the repair process, including the tools used, parts replaced, and testing methods. This documentation helps if the same problem occurs again and allows you to improve your repair techniques. In Nigeria, many phones suffer from a combination of physical damage from falls and water damage from rain, especially during the rainy season. These complex cases require systematic troubleshooting to identify all issues and fix them properly.

Class activity:
Students will work in pairs to diagnose and repair phones with multiple faults under teacher supervision.

Evaluation questions:
1. Why is it important to list all faults before starting repairs?
2. What should you do after each repair step?
3. How does documentation help in complex fault repair?
4. What are common complex faults in Nigerian phones during the rainy season?

Summary:
Complex fault repair requires systematic diagnosis, prioritization of issues, and thorough documentation to ensure all problems are properly addressed.

topics.title: Revision
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to summarize key concepts from the term, identify areas needing further study, and prepare for the end-of-term examination.

Introduction:
As we approach the end of the term, we will revise all the topics we have covered to ensure everyone is ready for the final examination.

Content:
During this revision week, we will review all the major topics from the term. These include advanced GSM repairs, soldering techniques, replacing components, troubleshooting advanced faults, flashing and unlocking, and complex fault repair. We will focus on the most important concepts and common problems that students often find challenging. For example, when reviewing soldering, we'll practice proper temperature control and technique. When reviewing component replacement, we'll emphasize safety precautions with ribbon cables. We'll also discuss common mistakes to avoid, like using too much heat when soldering which can damage the motherboard. Students should come prepared with questions about topics they find difficult. This revision will help everyone strengthen their knowledge and skills before the final examination.

Class activity:
Students will participate in group revision sessions where they explain concepts to each other and practice repair techniques.

Evaluation questions:
1. What are the safety precautions when soldering?
2. How do you diagnose a power IC fault?
3. What is the purpose of flashing a phone?
4. Why is documentation important in complex fault repair?

Summary:
Revision helps consolidate our learning and prepare for the end-of-term examination by reviewing key concepts and practicing essential skills.

topics.title: Examination
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to demonstrate comprehensive knowledge of GSM repair concepts through written and practical examination.

Introduction:
Today we have our end-of-term examination to assess your overall understanding of computer hardware and GSM repairs for this term.

Content:
The examination will cover all topics studied this term, including advanced GSM repairs, soldering and desoldering techniques, replacing phone components, troubleshooting advanced faults, flashing and unlocking, and complex fault repair. The written section will include multiple choice questions, short answer questions, and case studies where you diagnose problems and suggest solutions. The practical section will require you to demonstrate your ability to repair a phone with multiple faults, showing proper use of tools and safety procedures. You will be assessed on your diagnostic skills, repair techniques, and ability to document your work. Remember to follow all safety guidelines during the practical exam. The examination is designed to test both your theoretical knowledge and hands-on skills, which are essential for becoming a competent GSM repair technician.

Class activity:
Students will complete the end-of-term examination consisting of written and practical components.

Evaluation questions:
The examination questions will serve as the evaluation for this week.

Summary:
The end-of-term examination allows us to assess your overall achievement in computer hardware and GSM repairs for this term.

topics.title: Closing / Vacation
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to reflect on their learning, set goals for improvement, and prepare for the next term.

Introduction:
As we conclude this term, we will reflect on what we have learned and prepare for the vacation period.

Content:
During this final week, we will review your examination results and discuss areas for improvement. We will also discuss career opportunities in GSM repair in Nigeria, which is a growing field with many job opportunities in cities like Lagos, Abuja, and Port Harcourt. Many successful repair shops start as small businesses in local markets and grow into established businesses. We will also cover basic business practices for those interested in starting their own repair business, including pricing services, keeping customer records, and managing inventory. The vacation period is a good time to practice your repair skills on old phones or observe professional repair shops. Remember to continue learning about new phone models and repair techniques, as technology is always advancing.

Class activity:
Students will complete a reflection worksheet about their learning this term and set personal goals for improvement.

Evaluation questions:
1. What career opportunities exist in GSM repair in Nigeria?
2. What business practices are important for a successful repair shop?
3. How can you continue learning during the vacation period?
4. What topics would you like to study more in depth next term?

Summary:
As we close this term, remember that learning is a continuous process, and your skills in GSM repair can lead to many opportunities in Nigeria's growing technology sector.
